name: Valentine Cave, Lava Beds (California, USA)
relevance: Mars: NASA tested robots and rovers here that map a lava tube and search for life inside it, as a rehearsal for a mission to a Martian cave
source: NASA BRAILLE (Biologic and Resource Analog Investigations in Low Light Environments), Lava Beds National Monument

name: Cueva de los Verdes, La Corona tube (Lanzarote, Spain)
relevance: Moon and Mars: an 8 km tube with roof openings similar to the skylights seen from orbit; ESA trains astronauts there and sequenced microbial DNA inside
source: ESA PANGAEA-X (2017); Miller et al. 2026, Astrobiology

name: Indian Tunnel, Craters of the Moon (Idaho, USA)
relevance: Moon and Mars: lava tubes surveyed with lidar as a rehearsal for exploring lunar and Martian pits; their microbial communities were also studied
source: NASA SSERVI FINESSE; Weng et al. 2022, JGR Planets, doi:10.1029/2022JE007268

name: Kazumura Cave (Hawaii, USA)
relevance: Moon and Mars: the longest and deepest known lava tube (65.5 km), a size reference to compare with lunar and Martian tubes

name: Undara Lava Tubes (Queensland, Australia)
relevance: Moon and Mars: tubes formed by inflation of the lava flow, the mechanism proposed for the Martian tubes

name: Surtshellir, Hallmundarhraun lava field (Iceland)
relevance: Moon and Mars: analog astronauts lived for a week inside the tube, in the dark, with a test habitat
source: CHILL-ICE (EuroMoonMars), 2022 campaign; Heemskerk et al. 2020, EPSC

name: Lofthellir, ice cave in a lava tube (Mývatn, Iceland)
relevance: Moon and Mars: a lava tube with permanent ice inside; it shows the risks (collapses from freezing) and resources of ice-bearing tubes
source: Lee et al. 2019, LPSC L, abstract 3118

name: Manjanggul (Jeju Island, South Korea)
relevance: Moon and Mars: a tube almost 9 km long proposed as a lunar and Martian analog station
source: Moon et al. 2023, IAC-23 (Lava tube-based Lunar/Mars analog station in Jeju Island)

name: Warren Cave, Mount Erebus (Antarctica)
relevance: Mars: a dark, nutrient-poor fumarolic ice cave with microbial life fed by volcanic gases; a model of a Martian underground refuge
source: Tebo et al. 2015, Frontiers in Microbiology 6:179
